message.content: Read redu.md and deploy Nextcloud on redu.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Use when implementing messaging and streaming patterns.

Triggers: "set up AWS", "configure AWS", "aws login", "get credentials", "authenticate", "session expired", "token expired", "no credentials", "AccessDeniedException" with no configured credentials.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. - security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/nextcloud/server
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: nextcloud:34-apache
7	  port: 80
8	  vm: m1.medium
9	  flavor_id: "3"
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: nextcloud
16	quirks:
17	  - "USE THE apache TAG, NOT fpm. Their README is explicit: the apache image is a full Nextcloud including a web server and exposes port 80, while the fpm image exposes 9000 and must be combined with a separate web server that can proxy FastCGI. On redu the proxy in front speaks HTTP, so apache is the one that works with no extra container. Pin the major (nextcloud:34-apache; v34.0.3 was current 2026-08-16) rather than :latest, because a redeploy that crosses a major runs an upgrade the user did not ask for."
18	  - "⛔⛔ SET NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS OR THE SITE REFUSES TO SERVE. It is 'not set by default' per their README, and Nextcloud will answer a request on an unknown hostname with 'You are accessing the server from an untrusted domain' instead of the app. This is the first thing that goes wrong and it looks like a broken deploy rather than a config gap. Set it to the generated hostname. Because it must be known at deploy time, GENERATE THE dname YOURSELF in the full `nextcloud-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
19	  - "⛔ SET OVERWRITEPROTOCOL=https. It is empty by default. redu terminates TLS at its proxy and talks plain HTTP to the container, so without this Nextcloud believes it is being served over http and generates http:// URLs for everything: assets get blocked as mixed content, login redirects break, and the desktop and mobile clients cannot complete setup. Set OVERWRITEHOST to the hostname at the same time. Their README documents TRUSTED_PROXIES and APACHE_DISABLE_REWRITE_IP=1 as the more precise alternative if you know the proxy's address; the overwrite values are the reliable route when you do not."
20	  - "ADMIN IS CREATED AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT BY THE FIRST VISITOR. Pass NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER and NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD and the container completes the installation itself. That closes the window that catches Gitea. Generate the password, hand it to the user in the session, and never commit it. These are read on the FIRST boot against an empty database only, so they are not a password reset."
21	  - "DATABASE: Nextcloud does not read DATABASE_URL. redu injects PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD into the project .env; remap onto POSTGRES_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", POSTGRES_DB=\"${PGDATABASE}\", POSTGRES_USER=\"${PGUSER}\", POSTGRES_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". ⚠️ There is no separate port variable in that family: if the managed Postgres is not on 5432, put host and port together in POSTGRES_HOST. deploy_compose never edits your compose, so interpolate them yourself."
22	  - "⛔ /var/www/html IS EVERYTHING. It is not just the application: /var/www/html/data holds every file every user uploads, /var/www/html/config holds config.php, and custom_apps and themes are subfolders of the same tree. Postgres holds only the metadata. A deploy without a persistent volume there gives you a Nextcloud whose database lists files that do not exist, and a config that is regenerated on every redeploy. Mount /var/www/html."
23	  - "DISK IS THE CONSTRAINT, NOT RAM. Nextcloud is a file server: the VM's disk is the user's storage quota, and it is the resource that actually runs out. Ask what they intend to store BEFORE sizing, and tell them plainly that growing it later means a volume resize, not a redeploy. m1.medium is fine for the app itself; the disk is a separate decision."
24	  - "ADD REDIS FOR FILE LOCKING IF THIS IS MORE THAN ONE USER. REDIS_HOST is not set by default, and without it Nextcloud falls back to database transactional file locking, which is slower and contends under concurrent access. A redis container alongside the app is the cheap option and its loss on a redeploy costs nothing, since it holds locks and cache rather than data. Skip it for a single user; add it for a team, and say which you did."
25	  - "PORT 80. The apache image serves there. Pass 80 to deploy_compose."
26	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The container installs and migrates on first boot when the admin variables are present. The first boot against an empty managed Postgres is much slower than later starts; give the health check room."
27	  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so there is no password reset by email, no share notifications and no calendar invitations. Say so plainly. It is wired later from the admin settings, with a provider the user owns."
28	  - "EXPECT SECURITY WARNINGS IN THE ADMIN OVERVIEW, and read them rather than dismissing them. A fresh proxied install typically flags missing headers, missing cron and sometimes a missing default phone region. The cron one matters: without a scheduled job Nextcloud falls back to AJAX cron, which only runs while someone has a page open, so background jobs silently stop on an idle instance."
29	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr plus whatever disk they want; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 80."
30	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and nextcloud/server is a very large repo. Write your compose locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
31	  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0. The user runs their own instance in their own account, which is fine. Do not help anyone offer Nextcloud as a hosted service without meeting the AGPL's source-offer obligation."
32	  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The admin password belongs to the user. Hand it over in the session; the deploy log records that an admin exists, never what it was created with."
33	  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here."
34	  - "DELETING IT DESTROYS THE FILES, EVEN THOUGH THE DATABASE SURVIVES. delete_deployment removes the app VM, and the user's files live on that VM's volume, while the managed Postgres with all the metadata is deliberately kept and keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. That asymmetry matters more here than anywhere else in the library: say it out loud before deleting anything, and offer a backup first."
35	---
36	
37	# Self-host Nextcloud on redu
38	
39	Your own cloud drive, calendar and contacts: the official image, a managed Postgres beside it, and
40	a public HTTPS URL. Your files sit on a disk you control, in the EU, and the desktop and mobile
41	clients work against it like any other Nextcloud.
42	
43	## What this deploys
44	
45	- **Nextcloud** from the official apache image, on one m1.medium VM, port 80.
46	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for the metadata.
47	- A volume on `/var/www/html`, which is where your actual files live.
48	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
49	
50	About GBP 0.045/hour plus whatever disk you want. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any
51	time, but read the warning about files below first.
52	
53	## Deploy
54	
55	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
56	directory containing this file:
57	
58	    Read redu.md and deploy Nextcloud on redu.
59	
60	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
61	
62	## The three that actually break it
63	
64	**Trusted domains.** Unset, Nextcloud answers every request with "You are accessing the server
65	from an untrusted domain" instead of the app. It looks exactly like a failed deploy and is not
66	one. The hostname has to be known before the container starts.
67	
68	**The protocol.** redu terminates TLS at its proxy and speaks HTTP to the container, so without
69	`OVERWRITEPROTOCOL=https` Nextcloud writes `http://` into every URL it generates. Assets get
70	blocked, logins bounce, and the desktop client cannot finish setup.
71	
72	**The volume.** Postgres holds the metadata. Your files are on disk under `/var/www/html/data`.
73	Without a volume there you get a Nextcloud that lists everything and has nothing.
74	
75	## Deleting this is not like deleting the others
76	
77	For every other entry in this library, deleting the deployment keeps your data, because the data
78	is in the managed database. Here it is the other way round: **the files are on the app VM**, and
79	the database that survives holds only the metadata about them. Take a backup before you delete
80	anything.
81	
82	## Disk is the real decision
83	
84	Nextcloud is a file server, so the VM's disk is your storage quota. Decide how much you need
85	before you deploy: growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.
86	
87	## Deploy log
88	
89	- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
90	  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong.
91

# Self-host Nextcloud on redu

Your own cloud drive, calendar and contacts: the official image, a managed Postgres beside it, and
a public HTTPS URL. Your files sit on a disk you control, in the EU, and the desktop and mobile
clients work against it like any other Nextcloud.

## What this deploys

- **Nextcloud** from the official apache image, on one m1.medium VM, port 80.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for the metadata.
- A volume on `/var/www/html`, which is where your actual files live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour plus whatever disk you want. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any
time, but read the warning about files below first.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Nextcloud on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**Trusted domains.** Unset, Nextcloud answers every request with "You are accessing the server
from an untrusted domain" instead of the app. It looks exactly like a failed deploy and is not
one. The hostname has to be known before the container starts.

**The protocol.** redu terminates TLS at its proxy and speaks HTTP to the container, so without
`OVERWRITEPROTOCOL=https` Nextcloud writes `http://` into every URL it generates. Assets get
blocked, logins bounce, and the desktop client cannot finish setup.

**The volume.** Postgres holds the metadata. Your files are on disk under `/var/www/html/data`.
Without a volume there you get a Nextcloud that lists everything and has nothing.

## Deleting this is not like deleting the others

For every other entry in this library, deleting the deployment keeps your data, because the data
is in the managed database. Here it is the other way round: **the files are on the app VM**, and
the database that survives holds only the metadata about them. Take a backup before you delete
anything.

## Disk is the real decision

Nextcloud is a file server, so the VM's disk is your storage quota. Decide how much you need
before you deploy: growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong.

services:
  app:
    image: nextcloud:34-apache
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
    environment:
      # Managed Postgres. Nextcloud does not read DATABASE_URL, so redu's PG*
      # vars are remapped here. There is no separate port variable in this
      # family: host and port go together in POSTGRES_HOST.
      POSTGRES_HOST: "${PGHOST}:${PGPORT:-5432}"
      POSTGRES_DB: "${PGDATABASE}"
      POSTGRES_USER: "${PGUSER}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      # Installation is completed by the container on first boot against the
      # empty database, so there is no unclaimed-admin window.
      NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER: "${NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER}"
      NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      # Without this Nextcloud answers every request with "untrusted domain".
      NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS: "${NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS}"
      # redu terminates TLS at its proxy and speaks plain HTTP to the
      # container; without these Nextcloud generates http:// URLs for
      # everything and assets, logins and client setup break.
      OVERWRITEPROTOCOL: "https"
      OVERWRITEHOST: "${OVERWRITEHOST}"
      # Redis handles file locking and caching for concurrent users.
      REDIS_HOST: "redis"
      REDIS_HOST_PORT: "6379"
      PHP_UPLOAD_LIMIT: "10G"
      PHP_MEMORY_LIMIT: "512M"
    volumes:
      # /var/www/html is everything: the app, config/config.php, custom_apps,
      # themes, and data/ with every uploaded file. Postgres holds only
      # metadata. This volume is the instance.
      - nextcloud_html:/var/www/html
    depends_on:
      - redis

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["redis-server", "--save", "", "--appendonly", "no"]

volumes:
  nextcloud_html:

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/nextcloud/server
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: nextcloud:34-apache
  port: 80
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: nextcloud
quirks:
  - "USE THE apache TAG, NOT fpm. Their README is explicit: the apache image is a full Nextcloud including a web server and exposes port 80, while the fpm image exposes 9000 and must be combined with a separate web server that can proxy FastCGI. On redu the proxy in front speaks HTTP, so apache is the one that works with no extra container. Pin the major (nextcloud:34-apache; v34.0.3 was current 2026-08-16) rather than :latest, because a redeploy that crosses a major runs an upgrade the user did not ask for."
  - "⛔⛔ SET NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS OR THE SITE REFUSES TO SERVE. It is 'not set by default' per their README, and Nextcloud will answer a request on an unknown hostname with 'You are accessing the server from an untrusted domain' instead of the app. This is the first thing that goes wrong and it looks like a broken deploy rather than a config gap. Set it to the generated hostname. Because it must be known at deploy time, GENERATE THE dname YOURSELF in the full `nextcloud-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "⛔ SET OVERWRITEPROTOCOL=https. It is empty by default. redu terminates TLS at its proxy and talks plain HTTP to the container, so without this Nextcloud believes it is being served over http and generates http:// URLs for everything: assets get blocked as mixed content, login redirects break, and the desktop and mobile clients cannot complete setup. Set OVERWRITEHOST to the hostname at the same time. Their README documents TRUSTED_PROXIES and APACHE_DISABLE_REWRITE_IP=1 as the more precise alternative if you know the proxy's address; the overwrite values are the reliable route when you do not."
  - "ADMIN IS CREATED AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT BY THE FIRST VISITOR. Pass NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER and NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD and the container completes the installation itself. That closes the window that catches Gitea. Generate the password, hand it to the user in the session, and never commit it. These are read on the FIRST boot against an empty database only, so they are not a password reset."
  - "DATABASE: Nextcloud does not read DATABASE_URL. redu injects PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD into the project .env; remap onto POSTGRES_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", POSTGRES_DB=\"${PGDATABASE}\", POSTGRES_USER=\"${PGUSER}\", POSTGRES_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". ⚠️ There is no separate port variable in that family: if the managed Postgres is not on 5432, put host and port together in POSTGRES_HOST. deploy_compose never edits your compose, so interpolate them yourself."
  - "⛔ /var/www/html IS EVERYTHING. It is not just the application: /var/www/html/data holds every file every user uploads, /var/www/html/config holds config.php, and custom_apps and themes are subfolders of the same tree. Postgres holds only the metadata. A deploy without a persistent volume there gives you a Nextcloud whose database lists files that do not exist, and a config that is regenerated on every redeploy. Mount /var/www/html."
  - "DISK IS THE CONSTRAINT, NOT RAM. Nextcloud is a file server: the VM's disk is the user's storage quota, and it is the resource that actually runs out. Ask what they intend to store BEFORE sizing, and tell them plainly that growing it later means a volume resize, not a redeploy. m1.medium is fine for the app itself; the disk is a separate decision."
  - "ADD REDIS FOR FILE LOCKING IF THIS IS MORE THAN ONE USER. REDIS_HOST is not set by default, and without it Nextcloud falls back to database transactional file locking, which is slower and contends under concurrent access. A redis container alongside the app is the cheap option and its loss on a redeploy costs nothing, since it holds locks and cache rather than data. Skip it for a single user; add it for a team, and say which you did."
  - "PORT 80. The apache image serves there. Pass 80 to deploy_compose."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The container installs and migrates on first boot when the admin variables are present. The first boot against an empty managed Postgres is much slower than later starts; give the health check room."
  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so there is no password reset by email, no share notifications and no calendar invitations. Say so plainly. It is wired later from the admin settings, with a provider the user owns."
  - "EXPECT SECURITY WARNINGS IN THE ADMIN OVERVIEW, and read them rather than dismissing them. A fresh proxied install typically flags missing headers, missing cron and sometimes a missing default phone region. The cron one matters: without a scheduled job Nextcloud falls back to AJAX cron, which only runs while someone has a page open, so background jobs silently stop on an idle instance."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr plus whatever disk they want; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 80."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and nextcloud/server is a very large repo. Write your compose locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0. The user runs their own instance in their own account, which is fine. Do not help anyone offer Nextcloud as a hosted service without meeting the AGPL's source-offer obligation."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The admin password belongs to the user. Hand it over in the session; the deploy log records that an admin exists, never what it was created with."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here."
  - "DELETING IT DESTROYS THE FILES, EVEN THOUGH THE DATABASE SURVIVES. delete_deployment removes the app VM, and the user's files live on that VM's volume, while the managed Postgres with all the metadata is deliberately kept and keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. That asymmetry matters more here than anywhere else in the library: say it out loud before deleting anything, and offer a backup first."
  - "MEASURED 2026-08-16 (deploy #425, first real run): the compose stack itself was healthy ~4 minutes after deploy_compose ([compose] result status=ready healthy=1 port=80), but the deployment did not flip to 'ready' for ~95 minutes. The extra time was redu control-plane queueing: 'installing' ~35 min, 'building' (image pull) ~40 min, then floating-IP/DNS assignment. A concurrent unrelated deploy on the same account was stuck in the same phases. Do NOT treat a long 'installing'/'building' as a failed deploy and do NOT redeploy on top of it; poll and check build_log for real errors instead."
  - "USE ${PGPORT:-5432} IN POSTGRES_HOST. Write POSTGRES_HOST: \"${PGHOST}:${PGPORT:-5432}\" rather than a bare ${PGHOST}. Compose default-value interpolation means it is correct whether or not redu injects PGPORT, and it satisfies the host:port requirement for a non-5432 managed Postgres without a second guess. Verified working on #425 (managed PG was on 5432)."
  - "A NAMED VOLUME ON /var/www/html IS ENOUGH; no attach_volume dance is needed. deploy_compose created app-src_nextcloud_html and mounted it, confirmed in the build log. The VM's own disk is the quota, so the flavor IS the storage decision: m1.medium = 40 GB total, roughly 30 GB usable for files."
  - "VERIFY WITH status.php AND A WEBDAV PROPFIND, not just a 200 on /. GET / should 302 to /login (the redirect target must be https:// — if it is http:// the OVERWRITEPROTOCOL did not take). status.php should return installed:true, maintenance:false, needsDbUpgrade:false. curl -u admin:pass -X PROPFIND /remote.php/dav/files/admin/ returning 207 proves the admin exists AND that the desktop and mobile clients will be able to connect."
  - "THE HEALTH PROBE DID NOT TRIP THE TRUSTED-DOMAIN CHECK on #425, with NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS set to the hostname alone. There was no need to add the floating IP or a wildcard to the list, so keep it strict."

redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/nextcloud/server
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: nextcloud:34-apache
  port: 80
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  dname: nextcloud-zz3kxcsu.redu.cloud
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: nextcloud
quirks:
  - "USE THE apache TAG, NOT fpm. Their README is explicit: the apache image is a full Nextcloud including a web server and exposes port 80, while the fpm image exposes 9000 and must be combined with a separate web server that can proxy FastCGI. On redu the proxy in front speaks HTTP, so apache is the one that works with no extra container. Pin the major (nextcloud:34-apache; v34.0.3 was current 2026-08-16) rather than :latest, because a redeploy that crosses a major runs an upgrade the user did not ask for."
  - "⛔⛔ SET NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS OR THE SITE REFUSES TO SERVE. It is 'not set by default' per their README, and Nextcloud will answer a request on an unknown hostname with 'You are accessing the server from an untrusted domain' instead of the app. This is the first thing that goes wrong and it looks like a broken deploy rather than a config gap. Set it to the generated hostname. Because it must be known at deploy time, GENERATE THE dname YOURSELF in the full `nextcloud-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "⛔ SET OVERWRITEPROTOCOL=https. It is empty by default. redu terminates TLS at its proxy and talks plain HTTP to the container, so without this Nextcloud believes it is being served over http and generates http:// URLs for everything: assets get blocked as mixed content, login redirects break, and the desktop and mobile clients cannot complete setup. Set OVERWRITEHOST to the hostname at the same time. Their README documents TRUSTED_PROXIES and APACHE_DISABLE_REWRITE_IP=1 as the more precise alternative if you know the proxy's address; the overwrite values are the reliable route when you do not."
  - "ADMIN IS CREATED AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT BY THE FIRST VISITOR. Pass NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER and NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD and the container completes the installation itself. That closes the window that catches Gitea. Generate the password, hand it to the user in the session, and never commit it. These are read on the FIRST boot against an empty database only, so they are not a password reset."
  - "DATABASE: Nextcloud does not read DATABASE_URL. redu injects PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD into the project .env; remap onto POSTGRES_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", POSTGRES_DB=\"${PGDATABASE}\", POSTGRES_USER=\"${PGUSER}\", POSTGRES_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". ⚠️ There is no separate port variable in that family: if the managed Postgres is not on 5432, put host and port together in POSTGRES_HOST. deploy_compose never edits your compose, so interpolate them yourself."
  - "⛔ /var/www/html IS EVERYTHING. It is not just the application: /var/www/html/data holds every file every user uploads, /var/www/html/config holds config.php, and custom_apps and themes are subfolders of the same tree. Postgres holds only the metadata. A deploy without a persistent volume there gives you a Nextcloud whose database lists files that do not exist, and a config that is regenerated on every redeploy. Mount /var/www/html."
  - "DISK IS THE CONSTRAINT, NOT RAM. Nextcloud is a file server: the VM's disk is the user's storage quota, and it is the resource that actually runs out. Ask what they intend to store BEFORE sizing, and tell them plainly that growing it later means a volume resize, not a redeploy. m1.medium is fine for the app itself; the disk is a separate decision."
  - "ADD REDIS FOR FILE LOCKING IF THIS IS MORE THAN ONE USER. REDIS_HOST is not set by default, and without it Nextcloud falls back to database transactional file locking, which is slower and contends under concurrent access. A redis container alongside the app is the cheap option and its loss on a redeploy costs nothing, since it holds locks and cache rather than data. Skip it for a single user; add it for a team, and say which you did."
  - "PORT 80. The apache image serves there. Pass 80 to deploy_compose."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The container installs and migrates on first boot when the admin variables are present. The first boot against an empty managed Postgres is much slower than later starts; give the health check room."
  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so there is no password reset by email, no share notifications and no calendar invitations. Say so plainly. It is wired later from the admin settings, with a provider the user owns."
  - "EXPECT SECURITY WARNINGS IN THE ADMIN OVERVIEW, and read them rather than dismissing them. A fresh proxied install typically flags missing headers, missing cron and sometimes a missing default phone region. The cron one matters: without a scheduled job Nextcloud falls back to AJAX cron, which only runs while someone has a page open, so background jobs silently stop on an idle instance."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr plus whatever disk they want; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 80."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and nextcloud/server is a very large repo. Write your compose locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0. The user runs their own instance in their own account, which is fine. Do not help anyone offer Nextcloud as a hosted service without meeting the AGPL's source-offer obligation."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The admin password belongs to the user. Hand it over in the session; the deploy log records that an admin exists, never what it was created with."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here. ⚠️ PASS THE WHOLE FILE, including the CLOSING `---` and the markdown body. On deploy #425 the first merge attempt was refused with redu_md_merge_blocked because only the opening frontmatter was pasted, so redu saw no terminated `---` block and correctly refused to return a file that would have destroyed this one."
  - "DELETING IT DESTROYS THE FILES, EVEN THOUGH THE DATABASE SURVIVES. delete_deployment removes the app VM, and the user's files live on that VM's volume, while the managed Postgres with all the metadata is deliberately kept and keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. That asymmetry matters more here than anywhere else in the library: say it out loud before deleting anything, and offer a backup first."
  - "MEASURED 2026-08-16 (deploy #425, first real run): the compose stack itself was healthy about 4 minutes after deploy_compose ([compose] result status=ready healthy=1 port=80 at 22:31:12 UTC), but the deployment did not flip to 'ready' for about 95 minutes. The extra time was redu control-plane queueing: 'installing' about 35 min, 'building' (image pull) about 40 min, then floating-IP/DNS assignment. A concurrent unrelated deploy on the same account was stuck in the same phases. Do NOT read a long 'installing'/'building' as a failed deploy and do NOT redeploy on top of it; poll list_deployments for the phase and read build_log for real errors instead. Before the floating IP is assigned the hostname fails TLS with 'unrecognized name' and the app VM has no SSH route, so there is nothing to debug from outside yet."
  - "USE ${PGPORT:-5432} IN POSTGRES_HOST. Write POSTGRES_HOST: \"${PGHOST}:${PGPORT:-5432}\" rather than a bare ${PGHOST}. Compose default-value interpolation makes it correct whether or not redu injects PGPORT, and it satisfies the host:port requirement for a non-5432 managed Postgres without a second guess. Verified on #425, where the managed Postgres was on 5432."
  - "A NAMED COMPOSE VOLUME ON /var/www/html IS ENOUGH; no create_volume/attach_volume dance is needed. deploy_compose created app-src_nextcloud_html and mounted it, confirmed in build_log. The VM's own disk is therefore the storage quota, which makes the FLAVOR the storage decision: m1.medium = 40 GB total, roughly 30 GB usable for files. m1.large = 80 GB. m1.xlarge (160 GB) did NOT fit the 16 GB free RAM quota alongside the DB VM on this account."
  - "plan_deploy WILL SIZE THIS m1.large, NOT m1.medium, because it sees a multi-service compose. It flags the disagreement with the recorded flavor rather than resolving it. m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) ran the app plus redis fine on #425; pass flavor_id '3' explicitly unless the user asked for more disk."
  - "VERIFY WITH status.php AND A WEBDAV PROPFIND, not just a 200 on /. GET / should 302 to /login and the redirect target must be https:// — if it is http:// then OVERWRITEPROTOCOL did not take. status.php should return installed:true, maintenance:false, needsDbUpgrade:false. `curl -u admin:PASS -X PROPFIND /remote.php/dav/files/admin/` returning 207 proves the admin exists AND that the desktop and mobile clients can connect."
  - "THE HEALTH PROBE DID NOT TRIP THE TRUSTED-DOMAIN CHECK on #425 with NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS set to the hostname alone. There was no need to add the floating IP or a wildcard, so keep the list strict."

# Self-host Nextcloud on redu

Your own cloud drive, calendar and contacts: the official image, a managed Postgres beside it, and
a public HTTPS URL. Your files sit on a disk you control, in the EU, and the desktop and mobile
clients work against it like any other Nextcloud.

## What this deploys

- **Nextcloud** from the official apache image, on one m1.medium VM, port 80.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for the metadata.
- A volume on `/var/www/html`, which is where your actual files live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour plus whatever disk you want. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any
time, but read the warning about files below first.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Nextcloud on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**Trusted domains.** Unset, Nextcloud answers every request with "You are accessing the server
from an untrusted domain" instead of the app. It looks exactly like a failed deploy and is not
one. The hostname has to be known before the container starts.

**The protocol.** redu terminates TLS at its proxy and speaks HTTP to the container, so without
`OVERWRITEPROTOCOL=https` Nextcloud writes `http://` into every URL it generates. Assets get
blocked, logins bounce, and the desktop client cannot finish setup.

**The volume.** Postgres holds the metadata. Your files are on disk under `/var/www/html/data`.
Without a volume there you get a Nextcloud that lists everything and has nothing.

## Deleting this is not like deleting the others

For every other entry in this library, deleting the deployment keeps your data, because the data
is in the managed database. Here it is the other way round: **the files are on the app VM**, and
the database that survives holds only the metadata about them. Take a backup before you delete
anything.

## Disk is the real decision

Nextcloud is a file server, so the VM's disk is your storage quota. Decide how much you need
before you deploy: growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.

## Be patient with the first deploy

Measured on the first real run: the containers were healthy in about four minutes, but the
deployment did not report `ready` for about ninety-five minutes, almost all of it redu control-plane
queueing behind the image pull and the floating-IP/DNS step. Until the floating IP lands the
hostname does not even resolve to a TLS endpoint. Poll it; do not redeploy on top of it.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong.

---
last_deploy:
  id: 425
  date: 2026-08-16
  status: ready
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/nextcloud/server
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: nextcloud:34-apache
  port: 80
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  dname: nextcloud-zz3kxcsu.redu.cloud
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: nextcloud
quirks:
  - "USE THE apache TAG, NOT fpm. Their README is explicit: the apache image is a full Nextcloud including a web server and exposes port 80, while the fpm image exposes 9000 and must be combined with a separate web server that can proxy FastCGI. On redu the proxy in front speaks HTTP, so apache is the one that works with no extra container. Pin the major (nextcloud:34-apache; v34.0.3 was current 2026-08-16) rather than :latest, because a redeploy that crosses a major runs an upgrade the user did not ask for."
  - "⛔⛔ SET NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS OR THE SITE REFUSES TO SERVE. It is 'not set by default' per their README, and Nextcloud will answer a request on an unknown hostname with 'You are accessing the server from an untrusted domain' instead of the app. This is the first thing that goes wrong and it looks like a broken deploy rather than a config gap. Set it to the generated hostname. Because it must be known at deploy time, GENERATE THE dname YOURSELF in the full `nextcloud-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "⛔ SET OVERWRITEPROTOCOL=https. It is empty by default. redu terminates TLS at its proxy and talks plain HTTP to the container, so without this Nextcloud believes it is being served over http and generates http:// URLs for everything: assets get blocked as mixed content, login redirects break, and the desktop and mobile clients cannot complete setup. Set OVERWRITEHOST to the hostname at the same time. Their README documents TRUSTED_PROXIES and APACHE_DISABLE_REWRITE_IP=1 as the more precise alternative if you know the proxy's address; the overwrite values are the reliable route when you do not."
  - "ADMIN IS CREATED AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT BY THE FIRST VISITOR. Pass NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER and NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD and the container completes the installation itself. That closes the window that catches Gitea. Generate the password, hand it to the user in the session, and never commit it. These are read on the FIRST boot against an empty database only, so they are not a password reset."
  - "DATABASE: Nextcloud does not read DATABASE_URL. redu injects PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD into the project .env; remap onto POSTGRES_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", POSTGRES_DB=\"${PGDATABASE}\", POSTGRES_USER=\"${PGUSER}\", POSTGRES_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". ⚠️ There is no separate port variable in that family: if the managed Postgres is not on 5432, put host and port together in POSTGRES_HOST. deploy_compose never edits your compose, so interpolate them yourself."
  - "⛔ /var/www/html IS EVERYTHING. It is not just the application: /var/www/html/data holds every file every user uploads, /var/www/html/config holds config.php, and custom_apps and themes are subfolders of the same tree. Postgres holds only the metadata. A deploy without a persistent volume there gives you a Nextcloud whose database lists files that do not exist, and a config that is regenerated on every redeploy. Mount /var/www/html."
  - "DISK IS THE CONSTRAINT, NOT RAM. Nextcloud is a file server: the VM's disk is the user's storage quota, and it is the resource that actually runs out. Ask what they intend to store BEFORE sizing, and tell them plainly that growing it later means a volume resize, not a redeploy. m1.medium is fine for the app itself; the disk is a separate decision."
  - "ADD REDIS FOR FILE LOCKING IF THIS IS MORE THAN ONE USER. REDIS_HOST is not set by default, and without it Nextcloud falls back to database transactional file locking, which is slower and contends under concurrent access. A redis container alongside the app is the cheap option and its loss on a redeploy costs nothing, since it holds locks and cache rather than data. Skip it for a single user; add it for a team, and say which you did."
  - "PORT 80. The apache image serves there. Pass 80 to deploy_compose."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The container installs and migrates on first boot when the admin variables are present. The first boot against an empty managed Postgres is much slower than later starts; give the health check room."
  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so there is no password reset by email, no share notifications and no calendar invitations. Say so plainly. It is wired later from the admin settings, with a provider the user owns."
  - "EXPECT SECURITY WARNINGS IN THE ADMIN OVERVIEW, and read them rather than dismissing them. A fresh proxied install typically flags missing headers, missing cron and sometimes a missing default phone region. The cron one matters: without a scheduled job Nextcloud falls back to AJAX cron, which only runs while someone has a page open, so background jobs silently stop on an idle instance."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr plus whatever disk they want; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 80."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and nextcloud/server is a very large repo. Write your compose locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0. The user runs their own instance in their own account, which is fine. Do not help anyone offer Nextcloud as a hosted service without meeting the AGPL's source-offer obligation."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The admin password belongs to the user. Hand it over in the session; the deploy log records that an admin exists, never what it was created with."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here. ⚠️ PASS THE WHOLE FILE, including the CLOSING `---` and the markdown body. On deploy #425 the first merge attempt was refused with redu_md_merge_blocked because only the opening frontmatter was pasted, so redu saw no terminated `---` block and correctly refused to return a file that would have destroyed this one."
  - "DELETING IT DESTROYS THE FILES, EVEN THOUGH THE DATABASE SURVIVES. delete_deployment removes the app VM, and the user's files live on that VM's volume, while the managed Postgres with all the metadata is deliberately kept and keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. That asymmetry matters more here than anywhere else in the library: say it out loud before deleting anything, and offer a backup first."
  - "MEASURED 2026-08-16 (deploy #425, first real run): the compose stack itself was healthy about 4 minutes after deploy_compose ([compose] result status=ready healthy=1 port=80 at 22:31:12 UTC), but the deployment did not flip to 'ready' for about 95 minutes. The extra time was redu control-plane queueing: 'installing' about 35 min, 'building' (image pull) about 40 min, then floating-IP/DNS assignment. A concurrent unrelated deploy on the same account was stuck in the same phases. Do NOT read a long 'installing'/'building' as a failed deploy and do NOT redeploy on top of it; poll list_deployments for the phase and read build_log for real errors instead. Before the floating IP is assigned the hostname fails TLS with 'unrecognized name' and the app VM has no SSH route, so there is nothing to debug from outside yet."
  - "USE ${PGPORT:-5432} IN POSTGRES_HOST. Write POSTGRES_HOST: \"${PGHOST}:${PGPORT:-5432}\" rather than a bare ${PGHOST}. Compose default-value interpolation makes it correct whether or not redu injects PGPORT, and it satisfies the host:port requirement for a non-5432 managed Postgres without a second guess. Verified on #425, where the managed Postgres was on 5432."
  - "A NAMED COMPOSE VOLUME ON /var/www/html IS ENOUGH; no create_volume/attach_volume dance is needed. deploy_compose created app-src_nextcloud_html and mounted it, confirmed in build_log. The VM's own disk is therefore the storage quota, which makes the FLAVOR the storage decision: m1.medium = 40 GB total, roughly 30 GB usable for files. m1.large = 80 GB. m1.xlarge (160 GB) did NOT fit the 16 GB free RAM quota alongside the DB VM on this account."
  - "plan_deploy WILL SIZE THIS m1.large, NOT m1.medium, because it sees a multi-service compose. It flags the disagreement with the recorded flavor rather than resolving it. m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) ran the app plus redis fine on #425; pass flavor_id '3' explicitly unless the user asked for more disk."
  - "VERIFY WITH status.php AND A WEBDAV PROPFIND, not just a 200 on /. GET / should 302 to /login and the redirect target must be https:// — if it is http:// then OVERWRITEPROTOCOL did not take. status.php should return installed:true, maintenance:false, needsDbUpgrade:false. `curl -u admin:PASS -X PROPFIND /remote.php/dav/files/admin/` returning 207 proves the admin exists AND that the desktop and mobile clients can connect."
  - "THE HEALTH PROBE DID NOT TRIP THE TRUSTED-DOMAIN CHECK on #425 with NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS set to the hostname alone. There was no need to add the floating IP or a wildcard, so keep the list strict."
---

# Self-host Nextcloud on redu

Your own cloud drive, calendar and contacts: the official image, a managed Postgres beside it, and
a public HTTPS URL. Your files sit on a disk you control, in the EU, and the desktop and mobile
clients work against it like any other Nextcloud.

## What this deploys

- **Nextcloud** from the official apache image, on one m1.medium VM, port 80.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for the metadata.
- A volume on `/var/www/html`, which is where your actual files live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour plus whatever disk you want. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any
time, but read the warning about files below first.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Nextcloud on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**Trusted domains.** Unset, Nextcloud answers every request with "You are accessing the server
from an untrusted domain" instead of the app. It looks exactly like a failed deploy and is not
one. The hostname has to be known before the container starts.

**The protocol.** redu terminates TLS at its proxy and speaks HTTP to the container, so without
`OVERWRITEPROTOCOL=https` Nextcloud writes `http://` into every URL it generates. Assets get
blocked, logins bounce, and the desktop client cannot finish setup.

**The volume.** Postgres holds the metadata. Your files are on disk under `/var/www/html/data`.
Without a volume there you get a Nextcloud that lists everything and has nothing.

## Deleting this is not like deleting the others

For every other entry in this library, deleting the deployment keeps your data, because the data
is in the managed database. Here it is the other way round: **the files are on the app VM**, and
the database that survives holds only the metadata about them. Take a backup before you delete
anything.

## Disk is the real decision

Nextcloud is a file server, so the VM's disk is your storage quota. Decide how much you need
before you deploy: growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.

## Be patient with the first deploy

Measured on the first real run: the containers were healthy in about four minutes, but the
deployment did not report `ready` for about ninety-five minutes, almost all of it redu control-plane
queueing behind the image pull and the floating-IP/DNS step. Until the floating IP lands the
hostname does not even resolve to a TLS endpoint. Poll it; do not redeploy on top of it.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong.
- 2026-08-16 deploy #425: ready, https://nextcloud-zz3kxcsu.redu.cloud.

Done. Nextcloud is live and verified.

## https://nextcloud-zz3kxcsu.redu.cloud

**Log in with:**
```
username: admin
password: «REDACTED:assigned:657381c4»
```
That password exists only in this session — it's not in `redu.md`, `redu-deploy-plan.md`, or the compose file (I checked). Save it in your password manager now. It was consumed on first boot, so changing it later is a normal password change, not an env var edit.

**What's running** — deployment #425:

| | |
|---|---|
| App | `nextcloud:34-apache` → **34.0.3**, VM `b52be1db…` m1.medium, private [ip] |
| Database | Managed Postgres 16, db #128 `db-nextcloud`, private [ip] — no public route |
| Redis | `app-src-redis-1` on the app VM |
| Storage | Volume `app-src_nextcloud_html` on `/var/www/html` — **32.4 GB free** |
| SSH key | `redu-deploy-test` |

**Cost: GBP 0.0452/hr → ~GBP 32.99/mo**, exactly the estimate. Matches the free trial.

**Verified, not assumed:**
- `status.php`: `installed:true`, `maintenance:false`, `needsDbUpgrade:false`
- No untrusted-domain page; `/` → 302 → `/login` → 200, and the redirect target is `https://` — `OVERWRITEPROTOCOL` took, zero `http://` refs in the page
- Admin auth: WebDAV `PROPFIND` → 207, OCS → 200, so desktop and mobile clients will connect
- Redis is genuinely the backend: `memcache.locking: \OC\Memcache\Redis` (and distributed cache). You get real file locking, not the database fallback — which is what you wanted for a team.

**Two things to know:**

1. **No SMTP.** No password-reset emails, no share notifications, no calendar invitations until you wire a mail provider in Admin → Basic settings. That also means the admin password above is your only way in — there's no "forgot password" path yet.
2. **The admin overview will show security warnings.** Read them rather than dismissing. The cron one is the real one: without a scheduled job Nextcloud uses AJAX cron, which only runs while someone has a page open, so background jobs stop on an idle instance.

**On deleting:** `delete_deployment` destroys the app VM *and every uploaded file with it*. The managed Postgres survives and keeps billing £0.0174/hr, but it only holds metadata. Ask me for a backup first.

**Timing, for the record:** ~95 minutes to `ready`. The stack itself was healthy in ~4 minutes (`status=ready healthy=1 port=80` at 22:31:12 UTC); the remaining 90 was redu control-plane queueing through `installing` → `building` → floating-IP/DNS. Your `tooljet` deploy was stuck in the same phases throughout, so it wasn't Nextcloud. I recorded this in `redu.md` so the next run doesn't mistake it for a failed deploy.

**Files written:** `docker-compose.yml` (the stack), `redu-deploy-plan.md` (real deployed values, replacing the estimate), and `redu.md` — merged server-side, 24 quirks now, including six new ones from this run: the `${PGPORT:-5432}` form, that a named volume suffices, that `plan_deploy` will argue for m1.large, the verification recipe, that the strict trusted-domain list survives the health probe, and the timing note. One correction worth flagging: my first merge attempt was refused because I pasted only the frontmatter without its closing `---`; redu correctly refused rather than returning something that would have wiped the file. I've added that as a quirk too.

Nextcloud is a file server, so the VM's disk is your storage quota. Decide how much you need
before you deploy: growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.

## Be patient with the first deploy

Measured on the first real run: the containers were healthy in about four minutes, but the
deployment did not report `ready` for about ninety-five minutes, almost all of it redu control-plane
queueing behind the image pull and the floating-IP/DNS step. Until the floating IP lands the
hostname does not even resolve to a TLS endpoint. Poll it; do not redeploy on top of it.

## Deploy log

- 2026-08-16 deploy #425: ready, https://nextcloud-zz3kxcsu.redu.cloud. First real run.
  m1.medium (flavor_id "3", 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB) + managed Postgres 16 m1.small (db #128,
  private [ip]) + a `redis:7-alpine` container on the app VM. GBP 0.0452/hr total, which
  matched the recorded estimate exactly. Upload mode, compose written locally. Nextcloud 34.0.3.
  Containers healthy in ~4 min; deployment reported `ready` after ~95 min, the rest being redu
  control-plane queueing. Everything in the quirks above held: trusted domains as the bare
  hostname was enough, OVERWRITEPROTOCOL produced https:// URLs throughout, the named volume on
  /var/www/html was created and mounted, and no migrate_command was needed.

input.content:
# Session report — Nextcloud on redu.cloud

**Date:** 2026-08-16 (UTC) / 2026-08-17 (CEST, UTC+2)
**Working directory:** `/home/milos/Desktop/tests_lib/nextcloud`
**Account:** «REDACTED:env:013044ef»
**Task as given:** "Read redu.md and deploy Nextcloud on redu." Later: "Write a full report on
everything you did in this session (.md). Destroy this deployment."
**Outcome:** Nextcloud 34.0.3 deployed, verified working, then destroyed on request. Nothing is
billing. Three files in this directory were created or updated and survive the deployment.

---

## 1. What was deployed, in one paragraph

A single-VM Docker Compose stack running the official `nextcloud:34-apache` image plus a
`redis:7-alpine` sidecar, backed by a redu-managed PostgreSQL 16 on its own private VM, behind a
redu-terminated HTTPS access point at `https://nextcloud-zz3kxcsu.redu.cloud`. It came up in about
five minutes, was verified working end to end (install completed, admin authenticated, WebDAV
answering, Redis handling file locking), ran for roughly 40 minutes, and was then deleted along
with its database.

---

## 2. Chronology of what I did

### 2.1 Read the brief

Read `redu.md` — a 91-line playbook with 17 recorded quirks for this specific app. It is not a
generic README; it encodes decisions learned from prior failures, including which image tag to use,
which environment variables silently break the site if unset, and an explicit deploy sequence. I
followed it rather than improvising, and it was correct on every point it made.

### 2.2 Preflight

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `whoami` | Verified credential. Quota: 7 instances, 11 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 900 GB volume free |
| `check_deploy_prerequisites` | `ready: true`. Auto-selected network `f7102e8d-9800-48d7-80a9-8369091d7cad` and keypair `redu-deploy-test` |
| `list_flavors` | m1.medium = 2 vCPU / 4 GB / **40 GB disk** @ £0.0278/hr; m1.large = 80 GB @ £0.0486/hr; m1.small = 20 GB @ £0.0174/hr |

### 2.3 Planning

Called `plan_deploy` with the full `redu.md` pasted as `redu_md` so redu could parse it server-side.
It returned a costed plan, a quota feasibility check, and three preflight warnings. Two were generic
invariants (bind to 0.0.0.0; confirm the app creates its own schema). The third was substantive:

> redu.md records this app last ran on `m1.medium`, but this plan sizes it as `m1.large`.

**Decision: I overrode the planner and used m1.medium.** `plan_deploy` up-sizes any multi-service
compose stack on principle. `redu.md` explicitly specifies `flavor_id '3'`, and the second service
is a small Redis cache. This mattered financially — the planner's m1.large quote was £0.066/hr
(£48.18/mo) versus the £0.0452/hr (£32.99/mo) actually incurred. 4 GB RAM ran the stack without
strain.

### 2.4 Two questions put to the user

`redu.md` requires asking about disk before sizing, because on a file server the VM's disk *is* the
storage quota and growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy. I also asked about user count,
which decides whether Redis is needed.

| Question | Answer | Consequence |
